observations.trace: The strategic view resolves each inventory row to its item, selected worn placement and occupancy rows, deriving protected body parts from the selected placement. Tactical projection maps durable row IDs to entity IDs before building topology, clones catalogue and placement strings, generates tactical occupancy strings and maps attachment parents to entities. Tactical attachment selection resolves parent catalogue points, channel, tags and capacity; root ordering and fit recover fit zone only when item, placement and indexed location/channel match. The client follows parent entity and attachment-point strings through a bounded, cycle-checked ancestry to sockets.
observations.remaining: All producers, complete schema admission and client/native deserialization are not established. Missing catalogue or placement yields no fit zone in root_order, not necessarily an invalid admitted normal state; do not conflate catalogue, placement, occupancy, attachment and durable row identities.

observations.trace: The projected armor derives coverage geometry from the selected authored placement and covered parts from the strategic view. armor_layer_chain sorts by descending layer order, marks all geometry intersections, and selects the first intersection; armor_surface uses that selected surface. Thus multiple intersected layers and exactly one selected among intersecting layers are distinct meanings. The tactical log later reads the chain and causal aggregation counts intersections.
observations.remaining: A complete current provenance and scheduling trace for all armor producers and events remains open. TacticalInventoryItemId wraps a durable row ID but ArmorLayerContact and ArmorSurface expose optional u64; absence can be legitimate and a new wrapper is not justified solely by shared representation.

observations.trace: EquipmentSequence admits the full u32 encoding, advances with wrap and accepts a half-window; the first observation and initial zero revision have separate semantics. Server checks actor, sequence, revision and expected hand/destination before mutation. Disconnect and reconnect rebind ItemOf then explicitly rebuild held caches.
observations.remaining: The two-shield policy, all hook paths, scene loading, native scheduling and client life cycle remain open. Preserve actual unarmed timing, optional proxy, sequence wrapping and distinct stable IDs.

conditional_findings.severity: unassigned; source-derived conditional stale shield authority
conditional_findings.first_contract: A derived held-shield cache must stop granting shield behavior when its referenced item leaves the owner.
conditional_findings.trace: Assume an actor has at least two owned items, one held shield is the cached holding_shield, and its Drop action passes the authority, child, physical-shape and clear-space checks. drop_hand queues remove ItemOf before remove EquipSlot. Pinned Bevy commands consume the queue in insertion order, and the relationship discard removes the item from the InventoryItems collection; with another owned item, the target remains. The later EquipSlot removal hook looks for ItemOf, finds none and returns without clearing holding_shield. Normal remove does not remove the required quantity and properties; the dropped entity retains ShieldItem. InventoryView::equipped_shield directly queries the cached entity without checking membership, owner or slot, so shield_block_bonus can still return its positive block value while shield_holding_side returns None. The selected combat defense uses that bonus for interception decisions and accuracy; shield_aligned_response leaves a Block unchanged when no side is available. This is source and pinned-native reasoning, not an executed drop or measured combat.
conditional_findings.safeguards_and_limits: If the dropped shield was the only owned item, the relationship hook queues removal of the now-empty InventoryItems target; this witness requires at least one other owned item and no intervening cache overwrite or rebind. Drop has shape, collision and authority guards; no actual scene, successful drop, scheduler interleaving, exploit, player impact or every mutation path is established. A second actor pickup, dual-shield selection and other cache paths remain separate unresolved lifecycle cases. The historical pending q1555 identifies the cache family but did not establish this current consequence.
connected_repair_dependencies: After full audit and separate implementation authorization, align held-shield lookup with authoritative current ownership and held state, and make every ownership/slot transition update or invalidate derived caches without relying on removal order.
Trace rebind, replacement, despawn, scene restoration, dual-shield policy and all consumers; preserve legitimate unarmed and optional physical representations and transient tactical authority.
Later authorized checks should cover a successful shield drop with another retained item, empty-inventory behavior, transfer/rebind and any supported multiple shields; no product validation ran here.
conditional_findings.discovery: partial; source order, pinned native relationship and selected defense consumers established; actual successful scene, all lifecycle paths and aliases remain open

conditional_findings.first_contract: If matching tactical and autoresolve armor-layer distributions are intended to be compared, their reported keys and layer populations need explicit shared semantics.
conditional_findings.trace: The same MatchupSummary carries tactical and autoresolve causal summaries with fields named armor_layers_intersected and armor_layers_missed. Tactical logging retains a catalogue item string and material and formats the key as item_id plus material. Autoresolve telemetry retains an optional synthetic stable numeric inventory ID and optional material and formats those Debug values instead. The roster builds the synthetic ID from item ID and occurrence, while the tactical iteration fixture assigns separate sequential inventory IDs. Autoresolve emits one CombatArmor record for a body part, whereas tactical inventory can report multiple layers. Consequently these keys and populations do not by themselves provide a direct per-item cross-mode join even for the same authored armor; no report, telemetry or simulation was produced.
conditional_findings.safeguards_and_limits: Separate modes can intentionally expose different diagnostic views; the report may not promise direct per-layer comparison and no actual consumer or misleading output is established. The earlier PL13-ITERATION-ARMOR-PROJECTION concerns per-part stat overwrite and provenance on overlapping loadouts; it is related but has a distinct first contract and is not silently merged. Absence of armor and duplicate same-catalog items require explicit policy.
connected_repair_dependencies: Determine intended comparison grain and all report consumers. If cross-mode joins are required, retain a shared occurrence-aware authored item identity and clearly distinguish the modes’ different layer populations; otherwise label their scopes explicitly.
Coordinate with the separate historical overlapping-stat projection and tactical armor topology/contact issues without treating them as aliases.
Later authorized validation should cover same item, duplicate occurrences, no armor, and overlapping layers; do not run the iteration runner during this audit.
conditional_findings.discovery: partial; divergent source labels and populations established, intended consumer comparison and exact aliases remain open
